goal: Write a formal design specification for a permanent canvas-first desktop shell with a collapsible legacy sidebar, linked text-page references, a right multi-tab document panel, global AI conversation HUD rendered as a screen-space overlay, searchable conversation history and retained TTS interaction.
non_goals: Do not implement or modify runtime behavior in this task.
Do not replace the existing chat database, conversation model, RAG pipeline or TTS engine.
Do not duplicate note正文 into canvas nodes; canvas references must remain linked to source notes.
Do not turn chat messages into canvas entities or persist HUD layout inside canvas documents.
Do not remove existing file, note, canvas, editor, relationship, undo/redo or AI permission features.
Do not add mobile behavior in this Windows-only task.
Do not expose or modify the configured localhost AI credential.
acceptance_criteria: The specification defines a permanently mounted canvas-first home shell and preserves the existing file, note and canvas sidebar functions.
The specification defines a collapsible 320px-class left sidebar with a 48px icon rail and persisted UI state.
The specification defines hover preview, click-to-open right text panel, retained multi-tab editing, and drag-to-canvas linked note references.
The specification allows multiple references to one note, automatic title/summary refresh for all references and safe missing-source behavior.
The specification defines global conversations with per-message source canvas metadata and current-canvas-only retrieval at send time.
The specification defines a bottom expandable chat HUD whose transcript is screen-space, follows the dialog, does not pan or zoom with the canvas, and supports a searchable history popover.
The specification defines collapsed latest-turn preview, full transcript scrolling, loading states, session switching safeguards and retained TTS/STT behavior.
The specification contains error handling, accessibility, performance and Windows verification scenarios with no unresolved placeholder or contradiction.
context_sources: src/app/core/main/page.tsx currently bypasses the three-panel shell for canvas mode and renders only EditorLayout plus bottom ChatInput/ChatFooter.
src/app/core/main/left-sidebar.tsx owns Files, Notes and Canvases tabs and their existing actions.
src/app/core/main/chat/chat-content.tsx already renders persisted messages, loading, agent, RAG and TTS controls through child components.
src/app/core/main/chat/chat-header.tsx and history-dropdown.tsx already expose conversation switching, search, delete and new-chat behavior.
src/stores/chat.ts and the conversation/chat database own global conversation persistence and message loading.
src/app/core/main/editor/editor-layout.tsx and the note list/detail components own existing multi-tab text browsing and editing.

docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-25-viewport-normalized-content-scaling-design.md, docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-25-solid-canvas-block-collision-design.md define linked sizing, collision and placement dependencies.
notes: Use the fixed UTF-8 I/O baseline.
The user selected a right resizable text panel, hover preview after 400ms, a global conversation archive and a bottom screen-space chat HUD.
The user selected global conversations: each message carries source canvas metadata, while retrieval uses the current canvas at send time.
A linked note reference may appear multiple times on one canvas; all references refresh title, summary and timestamp when the source note changes.
The user selected voice-session auto-read for microphone prompts and manual read-aloud for ordinary text prompts.
Stop after writing and independently reviewing the specification so the user can review it before implementation planning.
